stories.title: November 1912 A Bakery In Moabit
stories.description: Berlin, November 1912. Before sunrise, in a working-class street near Moabit, Hans the baker is already shaping dough in the warm back room of a small neighbourhood bakery, where a brick oven burns with coal and the flour settles over wooden tables. The shop is run by a baker’s household, supplying nearby factory workers, craftsmen, shop assistants, domestic servants, and families with dark rye loaves, mixed-grain bread, fresh Schrippen, and a few sweet pastries. Beyond the rain-streaked shop window, electric trams rattle through the grey morning, carts pass over wet cobblestones, and workers hurry toward their shifts. Inside, the oven doors creak, bread crusts crack, coins change hands, and warm loaves disappear into paper bags. Hans works among these ordinary sounds, while the woman serving at the counter knows many customers by face and remembers what they usually buy. More than a century later, their voices have vanished, but the little bakery remains imaginable through its bread, warmth, labour, and the rain falling outside its door.

stories.title: Orsi In November Winter Is Coming
stories.description: November settles over Berlin, bringing dark mornings, crowded trains, rising heating bills, and the familiar anxiety of approaching year-end deadlines. While the humans complain and prepare ambitious plans for the coming year, Orsi, a small snail working as a data steward, approaches winter with considerably less urgency. He carefully dresses his shell in a knitted cover, purchases an unreasonable quantity of chocolate, and installs a little electric kettle beside his office desk. His colleagues discuss productivity, targets, and strategic improvements, while Orsi quietly investigates whether his keyboard can be operated without emerging entirely from his shell. He has no intention of resisting winter, only of becoming appropriately comfortable within it. After all, Orsi looks after data, and data usually calms down; there is no reason for a snail to panic.

stories.title: Hormus On Wednesday The Cloud That Looked Like A Cave
stories.description: On Wednesday, Mei sets out into the Computing Forest with Hormus, the immensely wise but occasionally undisciplined ancient horse spirit, and Maja, the little bee who faithfully carries one command at a time. Mei has a clear destination and hands Hormus something very close to a map, trusting that his thousands of years of knowledge will guide them there without difficulty. But somewhere between his enormous memories, spontaneous inspiration, and peculiar interpretation of directions, Hormus leads the expedition completely astray. Instead of reaching their destination, they discover an enormous, inexplicable piece of cloud that somehow looks like a cave, an achievement so strange that even Mei cannot understand how he managed it. She is shocked, confused, disappointed, and deeply frustrated, while Maja remains ready for her next command and Hormus is still full of ideas. Eventually, the Mushroom House team decides that since they have already found the strangest cloud in the Computing Forest, they might as well spend the entire weekend studying it together.
